Global Programme for Vaccines and Immunization 
BACKGROUND 
The Global Programme for Vaccines and Immunization, which was created 10 months ago is composed 
of three units, the Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI), the Vaccine Supply and Quality unit (VSQ) 
and the Vaccine Research and Development unit (VRD). Details of the programme and its component parts 
are set out in document E

summary.text: An Executive Board working paper (January 1995) reviewing the Global Programme for Vaccines and Immunization, formed ten months earlier from the EPI, vaccine supply and quality, and vaccine research and development units. It reports the subgroup's view that results have been excellent, that EPI's country role should be kept, that GPV can strengthen health infrastructure, and that public relations work can counter anti-vaccine groups.

summary.text: Continues the subgroup's conclusions on the vaccines programme, covering the cold-chain unit's influence, economic as well as political constraints on results in Africa, the need for clearer relationships with partner organizations, and how to bring new vaccines to all children. It also notes the programme's heavy reliance on voluntary funds and suggests raising the share of regular budget funding.
